headline: MTNL releases voting results from 40th AGM
summary: MTNL has filed the voting results and the scrutinizer's report for its 40th Annual General Meeting held on September 30, 2026. The filing complies with Regulation 44(3) of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015. Shareholders can now access the official outcomes of the resolutions proposed during the meeting via the exchange portal.
why_it_matters: Provides transparency on shareholder-approved corporate governance decisions.

headline: MTNL shares rally 17% on board approval for Powai property sale
hook: Asset sale brings relief to debt-ridden telecom
summary: MTNL shares surged 17 percent after its board approved selling a Mumbai Powai property to the Income Tax Department for Rs 891.53 crore. The state-run telecommunications firm is executing asset monetization to lower liabilities that reached approximately Rs 40,000 crore by FY26. For an Indian retail investor, this transaction offers a rare liquidity event for a heavily distressed public sector undertaking struggling with debt servicing.
whats_next: Completion of the property sale transaction with the Income Tax Department
why_it_matters: Asset monetization provides short-term cash for debt-laden MTNL.
winners_losers: MTNL holders gain / creditors partially relieved

headline: MTNL shares surge 17% on ₹900 crore land sale to Income Tax Department
hook: MTNL monetizes Mumbai land for ₹900 crore
summary: MTNL's board has approved the sale of its Powai Plot-C property in Mumbai to the Income Tax Department. The transaction is valued at approximately ₹900 crore. This asset monetization comes as the state-run telecom operator seeks to manage its financial position. Shares of the company rose 17% following the announcement of the deal.
why_it_matters: Asset sale provides immediate liquidity for debt-laden state telecom firm.
winners_losers: MTNL shareholders gain / No clear losers

headline: MTNL sells Powai plot to Income Tax Department
hook: MTNL sells Mumbai land to tax authorities
summary: Mahanagar Telephone Nigam Limited (MTNL) has finalized the sale of its property at Plot-C, Technology Street, Powai, Mumbai. The transaction is being executed as a government-to-government (G2G) transfer directly to the Income Tax Department. This move aligns with the company's ongoing efforts to monetize assets. The sale is conducted under SEBI (LODR) compliance regulations.
why_it_matters: Asset monetization helps MTNL reduce its significant debt burden.
winners_losers: MTNL gains / Tax Department acquires land
